$comment: Metadata key registry - the governed vocabulary for knowledge_entry.metadata stamps (docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md 6.1). Starter file from issue #36; issue #51 finalizes it and adds the CI test pinning it against the models, the facts schemas, and the tool-layer allowlists. The pipeline validates every stamp against this file BEFORE writing.

syllabus.$comment: PROSE CHUNKS ONLY (searchable sections of the syllabus document). The structured syllabus facts do NOT get their own row: they are embedded in the offering's representative section row as facts.syllabus (a facts-syllabus-v1 object - the schema file remains the extractor's output contract). One offering = one row; siblings point via facts.syllabus_ref.

event.$comment: freshness exception: reconcile removes events the source no longer lists

course_code.note: any separator/case form; the DB column normalizes to 'SUBJ NNNN'; the pipeline applies the same normalization before stamping arrays. Legacy alias 'course_id' accepted by the validator with a warning.

subject.note: the prefix alone (ENGL); REQUIRED whenever course_code is stamped - mechanically derivable

semester.note: wintermester is stamped to the year of its December start

professor.note: display only - NEVER a join key

instructor_slug.note: slugify() of the instructor display name, normalized to one canonical first-last direction (NFKD ASCII-fold, lowercase, hyphenate - see the shared pipeline _slug helper). COMPUTED DETERMINISTICALLY BY THE PIPELINE and stamped by the SAME shared helper on the cv row AND every section row so the cv<->section join key matches byte-for-byte; the LLM extractor must NEVER emit it. Both sides derive from the same `professor` display string (section rows carry no HB 2504 profile URL). Unresolvable instructor (Staff/TBA) => omit the key (NULL column), professor still stamped. KNOWN LIMITATION (MVP): no collision qualifier is implemented, so two distinct same-named professors currently merge to one slug; add a department qualifier (maria-chen-biology) in the shared helper when this is addressed.

credit_hours.note: semester credit hours; from the schedule CSV on section rows, from the catalog on course rows. Needed for F-1 full-time-load counting and multi-course credit budgeting.

session.note: sub-term within a semester: winter | flex_dec | flex_jan | flex_feb | flex_mar | flex_apr | flex_may | flex_jun | flex_jul | flex_aug | 8wk1 | 8wk2 | may | summer1 | summer2 | full. Derived from class_features/dates at ingest; distinct from `semester`. Drives the compressed-term staleness fallback (prefer the same session a year back).

campus.note: open list - scrapers never fail on a new code; a display-name map is added with the tool layer (issues #37/#38)

dayparts.note: derived from meeting start times at ingest: morning < 12:00 <= afternoon < 17:00 <= evening; weekend added independently for Sat/Sun - a Saturday 09:00 class is [morning, weekend]

unit.note: school/academic unit for contact routing; 'General / All' is the never-dead-end fallback

topics.note: contact trigger topics (tuition_gap, rent, mental_health, ...); topic->category fan-outs live in a topics config added with the tool layer (issues #37/#38)

target_institution.note: metadata carries the short code (UNT); the facts document carries the display name (University of North Texas)

event_start_epoch.note: UTC epoch seconds; display timezone is runtime.json DISPLAY_TIMEZONE

extracted_date.note: informational provenance ONLY - scraped_at must be the DB-write run's start timestamp, never this value

raw_hash.note: document-level sha256 of raw response bytes - links a row to its raw-archive entry

set_semantic_arrays.$comment: sorted before content hashing so feed-order jitter never flips content_hash; all other arrays are order-preserving (meetings, grading, prerequisites[].one_of, deadlines). Ship ONE shared canonical_hash() helper used by every writer.

telemetry_vocabularies.$comment: governed here so intent-grouped analytics never fragment; extend by PR

profile_keys.$comment: chat_session.profile allowlist - mirrors the onboarding question set; adding a question extends the DB CHECK in the same PR; values come only from closed option lists (major holds a program_code)
